# Step 2 validation: retrieval and comparison (council loop, from 2026-11-07)

**Status (2026-11-11): closed and frozen (D427, §19).** The open defects carried with it are in §17.

Alex, 2026-11-07: "好开始；我觉得这几次的循环很有效的逼近问题我觉得应该把他写成一个skill 你思考下怎么construct 然后跑这个skill". Run
with the `council-loop` skill (`.claude/skills/council-loop/SKILL.md`). This is a validation of Step 2, not an end-to-end claim:
there is no Step 4.

## 0. Frame

- **Objective.** On stored Step 1 output, measure whether Step 2 finds the earlier statement a new evidence item repeats or revises,
  and whether the comparison labels the pair correctly. Then read what the deduplicated dossier of three investment questions looks
  like.
- **Alex's decided contract (PRD §§5–6, Codex thread [16]–[21], answers on 2026-11-06):**
  - a search engine over the evidence returns the top 10 for {thesis, evidence};
  - the search covers the entity's evidence across theses (choice B);
  - Jev labels each candidate repeat, revision or different;
  - a repeat adds its new source, and any missing thesis link, to the existing record;
  - a revision keeps both records, linked.
- **Proposed pass line (not confirmed by Alex):**
  - retrieval: at least 90% of true repeats and revisions have their earlier counterpart in the top 10;
  - comparison: at least 90% of found true pairs labelled correctly;
  - wrong merges of different parties' statements: at most 2% of comparisons.
- **Reference system.** Production's Step 2: word-overlap ranking within one thesis, top 10 (`views/matching.rank_evidence`), with
  the existing Jev piece question (`views/jev_matching.PIECES`).
- **Ruler.** The frozen golden-v5 does not measure Step 2 (AGENTS §7.1, "what it does not measure"). The pair ground truth built
  here is an exploratory reference by independent readers. It is not a frozen ruler until Alex signs it, and it is labelled as such
  in every result.
- **Data.** The Flash K6b draw-1 forward run over 115 gold articles (`poc/data/clean-step1-takeover-2026-11-07/gold-k6b-flash/`):
  282 kept items with summaries, passages, party, dates, tier and thesis links, in forward order.
- **Out of scope.** Step 3's writer, Step 4, the UI, frozen production files.
- **Budget.** Embeddings (`text-embedding-3-small`) and Jev ($0.042 per M input tokens). Calls and cost are counted before any send.

## 1. Council A (independent design, then one challenge round)

The fresh Codex session is `01a1b870…`; its records are `council/a-handoff.md`, `a-codex.md`, `a-claude.md` and `b-*.md`. Agreed
design:

- **Reference pairs (exploratory, model-authored, labelled as such).**
  - Population: ordered pairs (earlier item, later item) from different articles, with availability set by forward article order.
    Same-article pairs are excluded. An item linked to two theses is one item, queried once per {thesis, evidence} association.
  - Candidate pairs come from routes that do not use the embedding search under test:
    - shared figures;
    - shared parties and named entities;
    - summary-word Jaccard;
    - same-thesis lexical rank.
  - Readers do not see which route found a pair, nor any search or model output.
  - Labels:
    - repeat;
    - revision;
    - same quantity, different party (a subtype of different);
    - different;
    - insufficient information;
    - and, for repeats, whether the later item is richer or qualified (D204's risk).

    Two blind readers label each pair with the same full source context; disagreements are kept, then adjudicated with the source.
- **Generator-miss control.**
  - Sample: 30 incoming items, drawn uniformly within three time strata (articles 1–40, 41–80, 81–115) with a fixed seed. Inclusion
    probabilities are recorded and the estimate weighted.
  - Scan: the reader reads the incoming item's full passages, then every earlier summary.
  - Audit: a random sample of unflagged pairs is re-checked with full context.
  - Expected to be inconclusive if positives are few; expand rather than claim.
- **Retrieval arms.**
  - R0: production as written, word overlap within the linked thesis, top 10; a new thesis has no candidates.
  - R0e: entity-wide word overlap.
  - R1: embedding of summary, verified passages, party, time and period; query of thesis description, outcome and period plus the
    incoming summary and passages; entity-wide; top 10.
  - R2: R1 without the thesis in the query.
  - Strict forward availability throughout.
- **Comparison.** Jev with the cross-thesis wording and full fields, tested first on the labelled pairs, apart from retrieval, then on
  the retrieved candidates. An uncertainty option is open; an uncertain pair is never silently called different.
- **Metrics.**
  - recall at 10 by type and by cross-thesis status;
  - the Jev confusion matrix;
  - false repeats by cause, over true-different and over predicted repeats;
  - the combined path (right target and right label);
  - the dossier per thesis before and after dedup, labelled a simulation.

  The 90% figures are discussion targets until Alex agrees.
- **Open for Alex:** what is saved when one item is a repeat of one candidate and a revision of another, or a repeat of several.

**Dossiers fixed before retrieval** (Flash d1 thesis ids):
1. Customer financing and backstops: clean-1, the revenue-sharing and credit-support model.
2. Competition: clean-18 (custom silicon and AMD) and clean-24 (inference-chip challengers).
3. Product roadmap: clean-11 (Vera Rubin volume shipping) and clean-17 (Kyber).

item.text: The records span several distinct experiments, and their scores do not all measure the same thing. I’m checking which results reach the final answer or a reader, and which only measure an intermediate step.

item.aggregated_output:
# The end-to-end census (D442–D444): result, 2026-11-13

**Answer.** On the seven graded questions, under the frozen judgement ruler and D430's eligibility, both systems agree with reader B on
one or two questions a draw, and **every eligible judgement in either system agrees with reader B**: no graded answer is lost at
judgement. Every loss is at opening: the question was not opened in the ruler's shape, or was opened for another deadline, period or
scope. The largest class in both is **an event question opened with a deadline other than the ruler's**; the memory question (q05)
was opened in the ruler's shape in none of the six draws. Exploratory: the clean arm's chain ran on 2026-11-10/11, production's draws on
2026-11-13 (03:29–03:46, D444).

## Graded questions, per draw (outcome by DESIGN.md v4, procedure 6)

| question | production q1 | production q2 | production q3 | clean u1 | clean u2 | clean u3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| q04 capex 2026 | **agrees** | **agrees** | not opened | not opened | **agrees** | not opened |
| q13 capex 2027 | unresolved (same question split by family) | unresolved (same split) | **agrees** | **agrees** | not opened | **agrees** |
| q05 memory 2027 against 2026 | not opened | not opened | not opened | not opened | not opened | not opened |
| q08 China H200 import | not opened (narrower) | not eligible (deadline 2026-12-31, AI firms only) | not eligible (same) | unresolved | not eligible | not eligible |
| q09 financing commitments | not eligible (a part of the total) | not opened (narrower) | not opened (narrower) | not eligible | not opened | not eligible |
| q18 Rubin Ultra in Kyber by 2027 | not eligible (by 2028) | not eligible (launch by 2028) | not eligible (launch by 2028) | not eligible (due 2028-12-31; same question split, decides nothing) | **agrees** | not eligible |
| q23 Ohio guarantee by 2027-06-30 | not eligible (by 2027-12-31) | not eligible (by 2027-07-01) | not eligible (by 2027-07-01) | not eligible | not opened | not opened |
| **agrees** | **1** | **1** | **1** | **1** | **2** | **1** |

Unresolved, two counts (the council asked for both, `council/mm-codex-3.md`): **by the design's order** (v4, procedure 6: an eligibility
field the readers leave unresolved gives "unresolved" before "not eligible"), production 4 (q13 in p1, p2; q23 in p2, p3) and clean 2
(u1 q08, u1 q18); **by the decisive reading** (a split that cannot change the outcome, because both readers already mark the due day
different, gives "not eligible"), production 2 (the q13s) and clean 1 (u1 q08). The table above shows the decisive reading; it departs
from the design's order and is disclosed as such. Neither count changes an "agrees". Disagrees among eligible: production 0, clean 0. Not graded but reported: production q07 agrees 3 of 3;
q01 agrees 3 of 3; q22 agrees 1 of 2; q03 not eligible (non-GAAP not named) though its band agrees.

**Losses by cause** (graded; each loss at opening, cause (a), so the fact-by-fact trace of causes (c)–(g) applies to none):

| | production | clean |
|---|---|---|
| not opened in the ruler's shape | 7 (q05 ×3, q09 ×2, q08, q04) | 9 (q05 ×3, q04 ×2, q23 ×2, q13, q09) |
| opened, not eligible: another deadline | 6 (q23 ×3, q18 ×3); by the design's order 4 | 3 (q23, q18 ×2); by the design's order 2 |
| opened, not eligible: another scope or part | 3 (q08 ×2 with a deadline too, q09) | 4 (q09 ×2, q08 ×2) |
| unresolved | 2; by the design's order 4 | 1; by the design's order 2 |
| agrees | 3 | 4 |

**What production does that the clean path does not:** it opens both years of hyperscaler capex (q04 and q13) in two of three draws;
it opens the Ohio guarantee in three of three (the clean path one of three). **What both get wrong:** event deadlines (Ohio one day to
six months late; Kyber moved to the reported new year, 2028; China a month early) and the memory comparison.

**Records.** Matching `matching/MATCHING-RESULT.md` (6 disputes, all ruled SAME by the third reader); eligibility
`eligibility/answers/` (23 controls, two families; 10 disputed points to both third readers: 2 agreed, 8 split along family lines, left
unresolved); the facts outside the readers' folder; the clean arm from `stage_b/result/control-count.txt`. Recorded cost of the census's
production draws $1.35 (ledger $1.77); the stopped draws $0.98; the slice $0.013. Limits: one window, three draws a side, different days;
a third-reader split along family lines on 8 of 10 points (the council-loop skill's recorded trap).

# Second Stage A of the clean ladder step: the result (2026-11-10)

**The six lines are still missed. One count is worse than in the first measurement: the due day is the same across the three
sends in 18 of 34 theses (53%), against 21 of 32 (66%). The counts the readers give are better on every way of reading them.
The class the change was built for, an event's answer, is smaller and not closed; the classes it did not touch are as they
were.**
Stage A does not compare the step with production (D400). By D401 and D408 the work stops here and goes to Alex.

The step as measured (design version 32): the request as first sent with an event answered in three outcomes (D409); the same
44 stored theses, three sends each; gpt-6-luna at medium effort.

- Sent: `poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-2026-11-10/run-2/` (132 sends, 204 calls, $0.1495 from tokens). 114 ladders (43 events,
  30 figures for the company, 41 for a theme), 16 declined, 2 refused twice by code (two sends of one thesis: a quotation
  reworded, and once a question that pointed at the item). 72 first
  answers were sent back, 68 of them for a reference not in the article's words.
- Read by two reader families with the form as it now stands (D410; the event rules), and by me, all 132 answers, before any
  reader's row (round log §69). Where the readers differ (63 of 915 marks, 7%), two third readers ruled, one of each family.
  **They agree on 21 of the 70 points.** The Codex third reader ruled 54 of the 63 marks failed; the Claude one 51 held. So
  each line is given three ways: only what both first readers fail; what the two third readers agree, with what they leave
  unresolved counted for the answer; the same counted against it.
- Generated beside this page: `report.txt`, `tables.txt`, `code-counts.txt`; `own-read-before-rulings.md` is my read of the
  disputed marks behind lines 1 to 4, written before the rulings.

## The lines, and the first measurement read the same way

| line | first run: both readers fail | second run: both readers fail | second run: third readers agree, rest for the answer | second run: rest against it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. no ladder asks another question (Q) | 0 | 0 | **missed: 2** | missed: 4 |
| 2. no ladder leaves a part unlisted (L) | 0 | 0 | **missed: 1** | missed: 6 |
| 3. no outcome with no rung or two (R) | missed: 7 | **missed: 4** | missed: 5 | missed: 14 |
| 4. no refusal without a justified reason (N) | missed: 1 of 17 | 0 of 16 | met: 0 | missed: 1 |
| 5. 35 of 44 theses right in two sends of three, 28 by a ladder | 36 and 30 | 37 and 32 | **missed: 34 and 29** | missed: 25 and 20 |
| 6. the favourable end the same in three sends | missed: differs in 2 of 8 theses | **missed: differs in 2 of 9** | by code | by code |
| 6. the due day the same, nine theses in ten | missed: 21 of 32 | **missed: 18 of 34** | by code | by code |
| ladders with no failed mark | 86 of 111 | 93 of 114 | 83 of 114 | 57 of 114 |

The first run as its single third reader ruled it (of the stricter family) read 11, 4, 16 and 2 failures, 21 and 16 theses,
49 of 111 ladders; with every dispute against the answer it reads 12, 7, 18, 2; 19 and 14; 40 of 111. The second run with every
dispute against it reads 6, 8, 14, 1; 24 and 19; 56 of 114.

**What can be said whoever reads:** line 3 is missed (four event ladders both readers fail), line 6 is missed on both counts
(by code), and on the two third readers' agreed rulings lines 1 and 2 are missed by three ladders and line 5 by one thesis.
**What cannot:** how many ladders are sound. The two families read the form at different strictness at every level (first
readers 60 against 90 of 114; third readers 54 failed against 51 held of 63), and a third reader does not settle it.

## The event answers (the class that was changed)

| | first run | second run |
|---|---|---|
| event ladders | 44 (24 yes/no, 20 in five states) | 43 (two or three outcomes) |
| with a fault both readers mark | 13 (five states for the company: 10 of 17) | 8 |
| R failed by both readers | 7 | 4 |
| theses whose three sends differ in shape | 7 | 1 (a figure filed under the company once and a theme twice) |

The four event ladders both readers fail on R:
- three write the ruling out so that a bar already in place when the article appeared can count as it (u1/clean-11 pass 2,
  u2/clean-3 passes 1 and 2: "have formally decided against permitting", "decided to keep them barred", with no "after the
  article's day"). The request asks for "after the item's day"; the model wrote it in about two answers of three; code's
  sentence carries the scope for every other decision and not for the model's own sentence;
- one asks about first shipments "during 2028" and answers "on or before 2028-12-31" (u3/clean-7 pass 1).
The other faults both readers mark on events: a regulator's decision filed under the company (5: u2/clean-3 three times,
u1/clean-11 once, and a lidar law filed under the export-controls theme), and one due day.

## The classes the change did not touch (as both readers mark them)

- **The reference** (10 ladders): the $119 billion already reported carried as what the market expects; an expected range of
  50 to 60 percent carried with no number, so the judge is told there was no reference figure; a ratio and a contested count
  taken as references. D411 decides the first two and is not built.
- **A figure's due day** (line 6): the same in 18 of 34 theses; of the 16 that differ, 15 are figures whose publication day the
  model estimates anew in each send (24 or 28 February; 31 March or 15 May), and one is an event.
- **Direction** (line 6): the same two theses as before, both a commitment's amount (acc/clean-1: higher, lower, higher;
  acc/clean-7: lower, higher, lower).
- **A company's quarterly figure laddered** (2 sends of one thesis; its other send declined it) and an industry quantity filed
  under the company with its fiscal year (1 send).
- **Declined in some sends and laddered in others:** 7 theses (5 in the first run), among them one declined as "not covered by
  any theme" although the investigation is into the company itself.

## Where I differ from what the two third readers agree (lines 1 to 4)

On one point: they both fail R on u1/clean-6 pass 3, whose ruling out I held because it says "After 2026-07-06"; their reason
is that it accepts a report of the delay as a ruling out. On the points they leave unresolved behind lines 1 to 4 (17), I am
with the reader who holds on 14 and with the one who fails on 3 (no ruled-out rung where the investigation can be dropped; a
decision "that Kyber will not ship until 2028" that the article reports as already made; a refusal for "no theme" of the
company's own investigation). On my read: line 1 two failures, line 2 one, line 3 six, line 4 one.

## What this does and does not show

- With an event written in three outcomes, the event ladders both readers fail on R fell from 7 to 4 and the theses whose
  three sends differ in shape from 7 to 1. That is what was observed, not a proven effect of the change: the readers' form
  changed between the runs, and each run is one sample of the model three times over.
- The event class is not closed, and it has more than one cause left: the model's own ruled-out sentence not bound to a
  decision taken after the article (three of the four ladders both readers fail); a question that asks "during 2028" answered
  "on or before" (the fourth); a question about 2027 with a due day at the end of 2028 (two sends of u1/clean-6, on which both
  third readers agree); and a regulator's decision filed under the company (five). (Council `jc` corrected my first wording,
  which said one cause.)
- It does not show that the lines can be met: the classes behind line 6 and most of line 5 were not changed in this round.
- It does not show that these ladders let the judge reach sound judgements: nothing here has met the judge.
- The readers' form changed between the two runs (D410; the event rules; mark F no longer applies to events), so the two
  runs are compared on what both first readers fail, where the form's changes bear least, and that limit is said here.

## The council on this result (`council/jc-challenge.md`, `jc-codex.md`; round log §69)

It recomputed the three countings and the event table from the rows and the rulings and read eighteen answers. It corrected
three sentences of this page (above): the due-day count is worse, not better; the fall in event faults is an observation and
not a proven effect; the event class has more than one cause left. The consensus it signed with me on what follows is in the
round log: the event class is diagnosed in full first, at no cost; then the figure's due day over its whole class; a third
measurement only on Alex's word.

# Third Stage A of the clean ladder step: the result (2026-11-10)

**Lines 1, 2 and 3 are still missed, by one to four ladders on the readings that favour the answer. Line 6 is met on both
halves for the first time; lines 4 and 5 are met on the readings that favour the answer and missed on the one that does
not.** By D401 a missed line stops the work and goes to Alex; Stage B is not opened.
Stage A does not compare the step with production (D400).

The step as measured (design version 34): the second run's request with code's sentence on the scope of a ruling out, the
reference's kind and range (D411), the tie rule for an amount the company owes (D413) and the due day of a year's figure set
by code (D414); the same 44 stored theses, three sends each; gpt-6-luna at medium effort. The code, the request and the
readers' forms as sent are kept in `poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-2026-11-10/run-3/code-as-sent/`.

- Sent: `run-3/` (132 sends, 155 calls, $0.1108 from tokens; spent under D401's $3: $0.755). 108 ladders (45 events, 27
  figures for the company, 36 for a theme), 24 declined, none refused twice by code. 23 first answers were sent back, 15
  for the reference's quotation (the second run: 72 and 68).
- Read by me, all 132 answers, before any reader's row (`own-read-before-readers.md`); then by two reader families with the
  form as sent; where they differ (67 of 870 marks, 8%, and 3 faults named outside the form) two third readers ruled, one of
  each family. **They agree on 21 of the 70 points.** The Codex third reader ruled 51 of the 67 marks failed; the Claude one
  62 held. So each line is given three ways, as in the second run.
- Generated beside this page: `report.txt`, `tables.txt`, `code-counts.txt`.

## The lines

| line | second run: both readers fail | third run: both readers fail | third run: third readers agree, rest for the answer | third run: rest against it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. no ladder asks another question (Q) | 0 | **missed: 1** | missed: 1 | missed: 9 |
| 2. no ladder leaves a part unlisted (L) | 0 | **missed: 1** | missed: 4 | missed: 11 |
| 3. no outcome with no rung or two (R) | missed: 4 | **missed: 3** | missed: 3 | missed: 11 |
| 4. no refusal without a justified reason (N) | 0 of 16 | 0 of 24 | met: 0 | missed: 4 |
| 5. 35 of 44 theses right in two sends of three, 28 by a ladder | 37 and 32 | 39 and 31 | met: 37 and 29 | missed: 25 and 19 |
| 6. the favourable end the same in three sends | missed: differs in 2 of 9 theses | **met: 0 of 9** | by code | by code |
| 6. the due day the same, nine theses in ten | missed: 18 of 34 | **met: 34 of 35** | by code | by code |
| ladders with no failed mark | 93 of 114 | 91 of 108 | 87 of 108 | 57 of 108 |

**What can be said whoever reads.** Line 6 is met (by code). Lines 1 to 3 are missed, by these ladders, which both first
readers fail:
- Q, one: u2/clean-8 send 3, a survey's rolling twelve months re-cut to "calendar year 2027".
- L, one: u2/clean-9 send 1 (the fine or remedies the thesis names are not listed as left out). On the two third readers'
  agreed rulings, three more: u3/clean-11 sends 1 and 3, acc/clean-2 send 3.
- R, three: u1/clean-3 send 1, u1/clean-6 send 1, u3/clean-7 send 1. Each writes the wait as the ruling out ("the end of
  December 31, 2026 has passed"; "no first shipment has occurred by 2027-12-31, so …"; "or calendar 2028 ends without a
  first shipment"). The same three I marked in my own read. The second run's four were another fault (a bar already in
  place counted as a ruling out), which code's scope sentence now governs: none of that kind is failed by both readers.

**What cannot be said.** How many ladders are sound: the two families read the form at different strictness (first readers:
70 and 113 of 132 sends with no mark failed; third readers: 51 failed against 62 held of 67).

## What the changes did

One send carried all four, so the run alone attributes nothing to one of them; each row rests on the small send or the
no-cost check that isolated it (round log §69). The due-day rule gives one day a thesis; it does not show that the material
is out on that day.

| built for | second run | third run |
|---|---|---|
| the favourable end of an amount the company owes (D413) | both ends in 2 of 9 theses | "lower" in 27 of 27 sends; mark F holds on 27 of 27 under every reading |
| the due day of a year's figure (D414) | one due day in 18 of 34 theses | 34 of 35; the one exception is an event whose sends ask about different periods |
| the reference (D411) | a reported amount carried as an expectation; a range with no place | 15 references of kind `last_reported`, each named so to the judge; the range spanned in 3 of 3; first answers sent back for the quotation 15, from 68 |
| the scope of a ruling out (code's sentence) | 3 ladders failed by both readers for an old bar counted as a ruling out | none |
| what is not a year's figure | the quarter written as a year's figure in 2 of 3 sends; the surveys written as "2027" figures | the quarter declined 3 of 3; the surveys declined 5 of 6, re-cut once |

## What is left, by class

| class | ladders both readers fail | where |
|---|---|---|
| a wait written as the ruling out (R) | 3 of 45 events | product events with a deadline (Vera Rubin, Kyber) |
| the object of a government's decision on the company's product (O; not one of the six lines) | 5 | the two H200 permission theses filed under the company; both readers want the export-controls theme |
| the reference of an event (XR; not a line) | 5 events, 2 theme figures | a year ("slated for 2027") carried as the reference's number; a present level carried as an expectation |
| a part of the thesis not listed (L) | 1; 4 on agreed rulings | no one pattern |
| the question re-cut (Q) | 1 | the survey thesis |

rung). Before that, on a figure question with no reference, it either picks the lowest rung for want of a number
(which its rules forbid: "not established" is never a reason), or reaches for a number the evidence does not give. Of
the twelve stored judgements not plainly supported, ten are of that kind; the other two count money already spent as
outstanding (financing, draw 1, 5th) and read the same figures higher (custom silicon, 4th, unresolved).

## What this means for Stage B (for Alex's decision; nothing is sent)

- The design's proposed lines would be: line 4, Stage B's UNSUPPORTED share among decided judgements at most 5 points above
  3%, so 8%; line 5, the share of judged theses whose last judgement is SUPPORTED at most 10 points below 100%, so 90%.
  Both margins are proposals Alex has not set.
- The baseline's faults sit exactly where the ladder step's questions are weakest: figure questions with no reference
  figure in their opening article (7 to 9 of 18 number questions in the unseeded replays, design §1; the fourth Stage A
  wrote 58 figure ladders of 104). So Stage B should be read per shape, as the design already asks, and a figure share
  compared with 8%, not the total with 3%.
- The baseline read every judgement alone; whether Stage B is read in the same shape is a choice for Alex (`BASELINE.md`).
- **How often the proposed lines are crossed by chance** (`line_chance.py`, `result/line-chance.txt`; the baseline's 16
  question paths resampled into tests of three draws; an unchanged judge and the same readers; $0):

  | theses a draw | figure share | overall UNSUPPORTED > 8% | figure UNSUPPORTED > 13% | median overall share |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 7 | 37.5% (the baseline's) | 0.5% | 16.9% | 3.1% |
  | 7 | 56% (the fourth Stage A's) | 7.1% | 12.6% | 5.0% |
  | 10 | 37.5% | 0.1% | 12.7% | 3.2% |
  | 10 | 56% | 3.8% | 8.1% | 5.0% |
  | 12 | 56% | 2.6% | 6.3% | 5.0% |

  The overall share moves with the mix of shapes alone (3.2% to 5.0%). The figure baseline is 4 of 52 (7.7%) with the
  unresolved judgement left out and 5 of 53 (9.4%) with it counted UNSUPPORTED; five points above gives 12.7% to 14.4%,
  and the table tests 13%: crossed by chance 6% to 17% of the time, since six figure paths carry the faults in clusters
  (and some are the same question in two draws, so the paths are not fully independent; the estimate is conditional on
  these stored paths, not a measured rate for Stage B). The yes/no baseline, 0 of 99, comes from ten paths. Line 5 cannot be resampled (0 of 16 unsupported last
  judgements); over 30 theses an unchanged judge whose true rate is 5% misses it 6% of the time, at 10% 35% (a binomial
  over independent theses, a hypothetical), and 0 of 16 is consistent with a true rate up to about 17% (a one-sided 95%
  bound). Leaving INSUFFICIENT last judgements out of that share can raise it; they are reported beside it.

**Council B (`council/km-codex.md`, `kn-codex.md`), consensus:** the result is reported correctly; both changes made during
the reading were made and disclosed correctly; the readers' agreement establishes agreement, not calibration, and no
control is known to be sound. A separate calibration round with borderline controls was proposed by the council and
withdrawn once the lines' chance behaviour was measured: an expected verdict for a borderline case would need independent
human readers and Alex's approval, not mine. **The recommendation:** Alex sets Stage B's lines and reading shape knowing
the chance table, and decides the paid Stage B send on the ladder step as it ran in the fourth Stage A; the test is three
Stage B draws read with the same form and controls, reported by question shape with coverage and INSUFFICIENT beside.
**Found since:** the adapter's mode that lets the frozen judge run over the ladder step's questions in a replay (design §5,
"the new mode") is designed and not built; a paid Stage B needs it built and tested first ($0).

## What it cannot show

- Anything about the ladder step's ladders, which are not in this reading. Stage A has not passed.
- 159 judgements of 16 questions: the first share is close to a count of questions (three questions carry every fault);
  the second has 16 cases.
- The readers are two model families; they agree on 155 of 159, which also means a mistake they share is not caught. No
  control is known to be sound; the planted answers are plain errors.
- One family's repeat moved once in three (a SUPPORTED re-read as INSUFFICIENT on custom silicon): the boundary between
  SUPPORTED and INSUFFICIENT on figure questions is where the readers move.

## Corrections to my own work, kept

- Before the readers I expected the eight later financing judgements of draw 1 to rest on the $30 billion; from the 6th
  they rest on a sound comparable (`own-read-before-readers.md`).
- The count refused seven rows that follow the form's second test (UNSUPPORTED with no rung to point to); the check was
  stricter than the form and was corrected before any count (`BASELINE.md`).
- Seven reviews went into the plan before the readers started; the first review found the controls could be picked out
  by a packet's shape, which would have made the readers' catches meaningless.

**Answer: by the rule written before reading, the difference is not clear.** Production covers two more of the five big matters both reader

three matters the clean path lacks are the company's own revenue and margin, which its request forbids as questions (D382). The second rests
mostly on one reader family: Codex failed 2 of the 4 judgements a separate reader had confirmed as supported, both of them production's;
both families call only one judgement unsupported, production's data-center revenue.

Material: 2026-09-22..28, 235 articles (232 never sent by any run), each system one draw from an empty library: the clean path
`poc/data/clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/week-r2/c1` (after D488), production `…/week/p1`. Readers: Codex (read-only) and Claude subagents, blind
to the systems and to each other; the keys are outside the repository. Model cost of the step (the one-day slice, production's draw, the

item.text:
**The evidence I reviewed points to two problems at once: the system does not reliably form the right answerable questions, and the tests have often been too narrow to tell which change helps a real reader.** For example, in one fresh week the two systems covered different important questions, but part of that difference came from a deliberate product rule; the judgement comparison also rested on just 7 versus 15 answers. That comparison could not fairly rank the systems. [Week result, D489](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:1>)

**Scope of this report:** This is an incomplete review, not the requested exhaustive history. I read the primary results cited below, but I did **not** finish the complete decision index, all requested design documents and logs, or every underlying attempt. I did not open `reflection-2/`, `reflection-3/` or `reflection-4/`. I therefore cannot honestly give the total number of attempts by class, a complete timeline, or a definitive list of things never tried. The table is a verified selection, with omissions.

| Date | Change and test | Result and status |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 29–Nov 1 | Extraction wording and closing review; gold articles, multiple draws. | The retrospective reports that one series reduced unwanted retained items from about 109 to 59 per draw with core and supporting coverage roughly unchanged; earlier sentence changes often traded one miss for another. Some versions were adopted; this is a grouped retrospective, not a count of individual attempts. [E2E log, section A](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:3>) |
| Nov 1, D253 | Increase preset questions from 10 to 22; three draws on the existing test. | Core items dropped without a question fell 21.3→19.3 per draw, less than the predicted fall to 14 or fewer. The 22-question set was retained for subsequent historical tests. [E2E log, row 1](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:26>) |
| Nov 1, D254 | Rewrite filing instructions to remove conflicting rules; three draws against the seeded control. | Core items reaching judgement rose 60.3→67.3 and supporting items 37.7→49.7 per draw, while estimated unwanted material rose 23.4→31.4, above the stated limit. Retained for that experiment, with the regression recorded. [E2E log, row 3](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:28>) |
| Nov 2–3, D268–D274 | Multiple prompt and structured-field attempts to retain useful evidence while excluding noise; selected stored articles, generally three sends each. | One field-based version increased unwanted material from 21 to 154 on one selected set. The v74i prompt was then frozen for production; these selected-case counts are not full-system results. [E2E log, rows 15–28](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:41>) |
| Nov 4, D361 | Give the frozen judge the reference’s source passages directly for three questions; three sends each plus controls. | Agreement was 3/3 for operating margin, 2/3 for capital spending and 1/3 for custom chips. The custom-chip result triggered the stop condition: supplying evidence alone did not reliably settle every answer. [Filing log, rows 20–21](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-04-filing-end-to-end/log.md:24>) |
| Nov 5–6, D378 | Split new-question and evidence reading into separate calls; compare with frozen production over the existing test, three draws. | Helpful matters: 156/156/159 versus production’s 166/170/162, at roughly 15% higher cost. The experiment failed its stop line and was sealed. [Current state, D378](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:88>) |
| Nov 7 | Clean Step 1: K6b prompt, compare models and effort on 115 development articles, starting empty. | Flash retained 205 and 197 of 234 helpful entries in two draws; production retained 167/171/162. This is evidence about extraction, not final answers. Flash became the preferred candidate. [Takeover log, sections 13–14](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/takeover-2026-11-07/LOG.md:605>) |

Alex adopted c8, but the test did not establish that the complete system could answer its own questions. [Current state, acceptance](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:3>) |

Two later readers left 41 of 48 disputed points unresolved. The full matching and judgement path was not run. [Lean log, section 49](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md:919>) |

The selected attempts fall into prompt wording and field changes, changes to which questions exist, a split or rebuilt architecture, model and effort changes, and changes to how results are read. I cannot count adoption or failure rates across those classes without completing the inventory. In the records above, the recurring failure is that improving one visible case can lose a neighbouring case; small samples and unstable reader decisions then make the size of the trade-off hard to establish.

The clearest results at the **reader’s end** are the Nov 4 direct-evidence test, the seeded and unseeded comparisons, and the fresh-week comparison in the table. They support a limited conclusion: both delivery and interpretation can matter, and a correct answer on a reference-written question does not establish that the system will create that question itself. They do not establish that either architecture is generally better.

The same questions have resurfaced. On Nov 1 the team concluded that filing, not extraction alone, was a major loss; on Nov 4 it again stepped back from filing to ask what missing evidence actually cost the final answer; on Nov 15 it again ranked losses by what a reader sees. [E2E retrospective](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:3>); [filing reflection](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-04-filing-end-to-end/log.md:24>); [lean reflection, D512](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md:405>)

A requirement was also missed: on Nov 5 Alex specified a library built from real material available **before** the test, and that an already-covered worthwhile topic should not be opened again. Later clean measurements commonly started empty; the current record acknowledges the mismatch. That makes those tests useful diagnostics, but they cannot represent the stated starting condition. [Current state, start-state and measurement corrections](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:103>)

**What stayed constant—and what did not.** The frozen reference and its July 14 endpoint recur, so they preserve comparability but cover a narrow window and a particular set of questions. Empty starts recur in clean tests; model families are also repeatedly used as readers, and the same families sometimes split consistently rather than resolving a disputed reading. The model and architecture themselves did change, so neither can be called constant. [Frozen standard, §7.1](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/AGENTS.md>); [full census limitations](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/CENSUS-FULL-RESULT.md:1>)

**What was never tried:** I cannot make that claim from the portion reviewed. The record I read does describe a *prepared, unsent* small comparison of the same articles with a real earlier library versus an empty one; it explicitly says no result yet shows that a carried library prevents failures. [Lean log, D559](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md:964>)

**What is the goal?** A reader should get worthwhile, answerable research questions, the relevant facts behind each, and an answer that the facts support as news develops. I would revise this framing if Alex’s signed design prioritizes a materially different reader outcome; I have not completed the required end-to-end design read.

**Is measurement part of the problem?** Yes: the empty starting state, narrow window, small samples and unresolved reader disagreements limit what several comparisons can prove. That does not make observed product failures imaginary; a larger source-backed comparison under Alex’s required starting state, with repeatable reader decisions, could show the present tests were nevertheless pointing to the right priority.

**How to break through?** Complete the historical inventory first, then test the same new articles against a real prior library and trace the resulting questions, evidence and answers through to a reader. I would change that recommendation if the remaining primary records show this comparison has already been run adequately, or if they identify a more consequential, independently demonstrated failure downstream.
